sugestoes.texto: WHAT: JSON.parse on attacker-controlled req.query.state has no try/catch. WHY: A malformed state query value throws uncaught in every OAuth callback/add handler, turning it into a 500/DoS instead of a 400. HOW: Wrap parse in try/catch and return undefined on failure.

WHAT: Single static header comparison gates overwrite of any userId/appSlug credential keys with decrypted attacker-influenced JSON. WHY: Anyone holding the shared secret can overwrite any user's third-party OAuth keys, hijacking calendar/video access with no per-user auth, HMAC, replay protection, or rate limit. HOW: See improvedCode; at minimum require HMAC-signed body with timestamp.
Falling back to empty string for CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY allows weak/misconfigured decryption instead of fail-fast. Require env var and throw if missing.

The comment requires 32 bytes for AES256 but the generation command `openssl rand -base64 24` produces only 24 bytes, so a user following the docs creates a key that disagrees with the documented requirement and will fail/shorten encryption. Change the command to `openssl rand -base64 32`.

Both @param entries say 'the app slug' but code uses appData.type as Credential.type and appData.appId as appId/slug. The doc for type disagrees with the code and misleads callers. Document type as the credential type.

Execution break: JSON.parse on attacker-controlled req.query.state throws unhandled SyntaxError on malformed input, crashing OAuth callback instead of returning undefined/400. Same pattern in encodeOAuthState.

issues.descricao: Claims the JSDoc describes appData.type as 'the app slug', copied from appData.appId.
Claims the team-credential branch only checks accepted membership instead of admin rights, letting non-admin members create team credentials.
Claims malformed OAuth state makes JSON.parse throw and crash OAuth callbacks with a 500.
Claims the Office365 video adapter passes the wrong app slug 'msteams' to refreshOAuthTokens.
createOAuthAppCredential only verifies team membership, not admin access, before creating a team credential, so any team member can install OAuth apps for the team via a crafted state.
The app-credential webhook decrypts keys with CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY falling back to an empty string when the env var is unset, instead of failing fast.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The "lost_access"/"go_back" toggle Button inside the disable <Form> has no type="button" so it acts as a submit. WHY: Clicking it toggles the view and simultaneously fires handleDisable with stale/empty codes, causing spurious disable attempts and confusing error states. HOW: Add type="button" to the toggle (and cancel) buttons inside the Form.
Same as login path: backup code verified with backupCodes.indexOf (===) instead of constant-time compare, leaking timing. Iterate and compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual.

issues.descricao: Claims a caller of the changed TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable still passes two arguments, but that caller uses a different, unchanged API module.
The enable-2FA test asserts toBeTruthy on the un-awaited isChecked() Promise, so it passes regardless of the switch state, including now that the backup-codes step is never dismissed.
Backup codes are compared with indexOf/=== instead of a constant-time comparison, theoretically leaking timing information.
Suggests a clearer post-2FA redirect journey in a file that does not exist.
Claims a 2FA page leaks a polling interval; no such page or interval exists.
Reports no issue.
The first 2FA e2e test asserts toBeTruthy() on an unawaited isChecked() Promise, so it always passes even though the backup-codes step now keeps 2FA unchecked until Close is clicked.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: request.referer is reflected unescaped into a JS string and used as postMessage targetOrigin. WHY: a referer containing quote or </script> breaks out to reflected XSS, and a full URL with path is an invalid targetOrigin so resize messaging fails. HOW: escape with j() and pass only origin (scheme://host[:port]).

request.referer is attacker-controlled (Referer header) and interpolated into a single-quoted JS string without JS escaping, allowing quote-breakout and XSS inside the embed layout. Apply escape_javascript (j) helper.

Second arg to postMessage must be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full request.referer which includes path/query. As written the targetOrigin never matches e.origin checked in embed.js, so the discourse-resize message is dropped and the iframe height is never updated. Send only the origin derived from the referer.

Controller no longer calls TopicRetriever directly — it does Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and the RetrieveTopic job calls the retriever later. The spec still mocks TopicRetriever.new/retrieve around GET, so it will fail. Update the spec to expect the enqueue instead of the synchronous retriever call.

issues.descricao: Claims embed.js throws a TypeError when the page lacks the #discourse-comments element because comments.appendChild is called on null.
Claims the embed controller spec fails because EmbedController#best only enqueues a Sidekiq job and never constructs TopicRetriever during the request.
The hourly PollFeed job always fetches and processes the full feed without a conditional GET; the feed_key helper meant for that is defined but never used.
States that the link fallback in PollFeed is correct; no problem is reported.
States the raw_html cook_method comparison in Post#cook is safe; no problem is reported.
States the cook_method assignment in PostCreator is correct; no problem is reported.
States the `if topic_id` check in EmbedController is safe; no problem is reported.
Describes the host checks in ensure_embeddable without reporting a problem.
States content_sha1 and absolutize_urls in TopicEmbed are correct; no problem is reported.
States the TopicRetriever throttle uses setnx and an explicit no_throttle check; no problem is reported.
Claims import_remote passes an unvalidated user-supplied URL to Kernel#open, allowing command execution with '|' or local file reads.
Claims PollFeed fetches SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validation, letting whoever controls that setting make the server request arbitrary internal or external URLs.
Claims the embed best.html.erb template closes its if block with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby, so every render raises a SyntaxError.
The embed layout interpolates request.referer into an inline JavaScript string with only HTML escaping, so a referer containing a quote can break out of the string and run script.
Claims postMessage drops the resize message because targetOrigin is the full referer URL rather than just the origin, breaking iframe auto-resize.
Claims setting X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL on the embed endpoint disables clickjacking protection and that the referer check can be spoofed.
Claims the cook_method migration default of 1 equals raw_html, so every post would skip cooking and sanitization.
Claims the 'not a url' TopicRetriever spec passes regardless of the InvalidURIError rescue because embeddable_host is blank.
`<%- end if %>` in embed/best.html.erb is not valid Ruby, so the template raises a SyntaxError and the embed page fails to render.
Claims `<%- end if %>` leaves a dangling if modifier that makes the logo output the condition, so the logo renders before the header button.
Claims the embed best action builds the view for current_user and then marks it publicly cacheable, so a staff member's view could be served to anonymous visitors.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: record_for_host returns false on failure but callers use eh.try(:category_id), and try only guards nil so false.try(:category_id) dispatches to FalseClass and raises. WHY: TopicEmbed.import (app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-43) crashes on malformed/unknown embed URLs instead of handling nil category. HOW: return nil instead of false consistently.

WHAT: _hydrateEmbedded calls obj[k].map unconditionally for *_ids keys. WHY: a null/missing ids payload (e.g. embeddable_host_ids: null) throws TypeError and breaks store hydration for that record. HOW: coerce to empty array before mapping.

WHAT: every embed comment/retriever check now does a SELECT via record_for_host instead of the previous in-memory SiteSetting string check. WHY: adds a DB round-trip to the hot unauthenticated embed path on every request, increasing latency and DB load. HOW: cache the host list with expiry and invalidate on EmbeddableHost save/destroy.

issues.descricao: Claims expandable_first_post? lost its 'embeddable hosts configured' guard and now expands first posts when no EmbeddableHost exists.
Claims the plural *_ids hydration branch crashes on non-array values and keeps undefined entries for missing ids.
Claims Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing, so the client's saveChanges appears to succeed without saving.
Claims EmbeddingSerializer emits only embeddable_host_ids without sideloading the host records, so the admin host table renders empty.

_hydrateEmbedded now treats every `_ids` key as an embedded collection: it calls `.map` without a null/array check (TypeError on null) and always deletes the original key, replacing real id arrays with undefined lookups when the root has no matching collection.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: order() copies $val verbatim into -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group, but legacy ordinal-group is 1-based while modern order is 0-based (ordinal-group = order + 1). WHY: flex item ordering diverges on legacy -webkit-box/-moz-box engines — e.g. @include order(2) in topic.scss and order(3) in header.scss render as order 1 and 2 there, breaking intended visual order. HOW: emit $val + 1 for the box-ordinal-group prefixes while keeping order/$val and -ms-flex-order/-webkit-order as $val.

Legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-indexed (1 == order:0), so they must be $val+1 to agree with order:$val. As written, legacy engines render order N as N-1, disagreeing with the modern properties and breaking ordering vs default-order siblings.

Legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group / -moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based (default 1) while order is 0-based (default 0), so copying $val verbatim is off by one on old engines: e.g. order(2) renders as order 1. Add 1 for the box variants.

issues.descricao: Claims the order mixin's box-ordinal-group values are off by one versus order, so legacy WebKit/Firefox render a different item order.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: API URL download limit changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` to hardcoded `10.megabytes`. WHY: Attacker via API can force server-side fetch up to 10MB even when admin configured a much lower limit, amplifying bandwidth/disk usage and feeding the 5x ImageMagick loop for DoS. HOW: Restore setting-based cap or use `min(10.megabytes, setting)` if a transitional grace is needed.

issues.descricao: Claims the API URL download limit changed from max_image_size_kb to a hardcoded 10 MB, amplifying SSRF bandwidth.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: add_members splits on comma without stripping whitespace so "a, b" looks up " b" which misses. WHY: multi-user adds from the UI silently skip members whose lookup fails, leaving the group incomplete. HOW: strip each username before find_by_username.
Route PUT /admin/groups/:id/members supplies :id, not :group_id, so require(:group_id) raises ParameterMissing on real requests. Accept :id (or both) to match the route and JS caller.
Route DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members supplies :id, not :group_id, so require(:group_id) raises ParameterMissing on real requests. Accept :id (or both) to match the route and JS caller.

Route `put "members"` under `resources :groups` supplies `params[:id]`; `add_members` requires `params[:group_id]` and will raise ParameterMissing on every real request. Use `params[:id]` (as `update`/`destroy` do) or add `group_id` to the route.

Route `delete "members"` under `resources :groups` supplies `params[:id]`; `remove_member` requires `params[:group_id]` and will raise ParameterMissing on every real request. Use `params[:id]` (as `update`/`destroy` do) or add `group_id` to the route.
Next clamps to user_count, which is past the last page when count is a multiple of limit (e.g. count 100, limit 50, offset 50 -> 100 empty). Clamp to (totalPages-1)*limit instead.

add_members looks up params.require(:group_id) but the member route and frontend URL '/admin/groups/:id/members.json' supply :id, so every call raises ActionController::ParameterMissing instead of adding members. Use :id (or accept either).

remove_member looks up params.require(:group_id) but the member route and frontend URL '/admin/groups/:id/members.json' supply :id, so every call raises ActionController::ParameterMissing instead of removing the member. Use :id (or accept either).

issues.descricao: Claims the now-unawaited findMembers() call creates a race where the controller has no member data available when it needs it.
Claims the public group members template iterates a bare members property that resolves to undefined because the controller's model is now the Group object.
Claims add_members/remove_member read params[:group_id] while the route supplies the group id as params[:id], so the actions always fail with ParameterMissing.
Claims add_members does not strip whitespace around comma-separated usernames, so entries like 'alice, bob' silently fail to add members.
Claims the public members endpoint accepts an unbounded or negative limit/offset, letting a caller force loading and serializing the whole membership of a large group.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym is called before .uniq.compact, so a nil/blank default raises NoMethodError instead of being compacted away. WHY: During boot/DB outage default_locale is not guaranteed loaded (per PR description), so every fallback lookup and every request via ensure_loaded! crashes instead of falling back to :en. HOW: Compact/map safely, e.g. [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en].map{|l| l.try(:to_sym)}.compact.uniq.

WHAT: Raw request locale (user-controlled via User#effective_locale) is returned unsanitized in the fallback chain and interpolated into Regexp.new("\\.#{locale}\\.yml$") in load_locale. WHY: An attacker who sets locale to a regex metachar string (e.g. ".*") matches every file in I18n.load_path, forcing the server to load all locale files into memory on their request (resource exhaustion) and broadening the file-load surface. HOW: Normalize/allowlist the locale (to_sym + check against LocaleSiteSetting.supported_locales, fallback to :en) before returning it and before building the grep Regexp (use Regexp.escape).

WHAT: set_locale now synchronously loads up to 3 locale YAML files via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! on every request, and FallbackLocaleList#[] hits SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback-miss lookup. WHY: First requests after boot/change block the request path on file I/O under LOAD_MUTEX, and every missing translation pays a SiteSetting lookup plus up to 3 backend lookups, amplifying hot-path cost. HOW: Memoize the resolved default locale per request/boot and keep per-request ensure_loaded! cheap (rely on @loaded_locales check), or preload fallbacks outside the request path.

SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym is evaluated before .compact, so if default_locale is nil the fallback lookup raises NoMethodError instead of falling back to [:en]. Compact first, then convert to symbols.

issues.descricao: Claims a fallback value cached for a not-yet-loaded locale stays stale after that locale's file is loaded, because ensure_loaded! does not invalidate the translation cache.
Suggests normalizing the locale because a String locale mixed with Symbol fallback entries defeats uniq and causes double lookups or double loading.
Claims a nil default_locale makes FallbackLocaleList#[] raise NoMethodError on every missing translation.
Claims every fallback lookup hits the database or Redis through SiteSetting.default_locale, amplifying per-request load.
Claims a user-controlled locale with regex metacharacters reaches load_locale's Regexp and forces loading of unintended locale files.
Claims @loaded_locales is lazily initialized and shared across threads without synchronization.
I18n.ensure_loaded! reads and initializes @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX, racing with reload!/load_locale under concurrent requests.
Claims set_locale's `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` (application_controller.rb:159) raises NoMethodError on every request if I18n.fallbacks is not the custom FallbackLocaleList.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever rowsAffected==0, which includes an existing device_id whose updated_at is older than 30 days (outside the BETWEEN window). WHY: A returning device after expiry can never re-register when the limit is hit, even though it is an update not a new device, and not-found is conflated with limit-reached.

WHAT: ProvideAnonDBStore now requires a bare int64 deviceLimit but pkg/server/wire.go still lists it as a provider with no int64 binding. WHY: Wire cannot resolve the bare int64 dependency (only construction site passing cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit is manual in impl.go), so generation/build breaks or creates a duplicate store with divergent limits.

issues.descricao: Claims ProvideAnonDBStore's new int64 parameter breaks wire dependency injection because wire.go still registers it.
Claims updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached for any zero-row update, conflating missing or stale devices with the limit being reached.
Claims anonymous clients can bypass the device limit by omitting the X-Grafana-Device-Id header.
Claims anonymous authentication now fails entirely when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, instead of the previous non-blocking async tagging.
Claims TagDevice now propagates all tagging errors instead of only the limit error, breaking callers that ignored them.
Claims updateDevice's time window is based on device.UpdatedAt rather than time.Now(), which may not match the intended logic.
ProvideAnonDBStore gained an int64 deviceLimit parameter but is still registered as a wire provider in pkg/server/wire.go, which has no provider for int64, so wire generation or compilation fails.

ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit but is still registered as a Wire provider (with an AnonStore bind) in pkg/server/wire.go; Wire cannot supply an int64, so DI generation and the server build fail.
Claims updateDevice's RowsAffected()==0 check wrongly denies already-registered devices on MySQL because MySQL reports changed rather than matched rows.
CreateOrUpdateDevice runs a full COUNT over the 30-day anon_device table on every anonymous request when a device limit is set.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware creates one MetricsMiddleware and mutates its next field on every CreateClientMiddleware call instead of returning a new instance. WHY: The middlewares slice is reused to build many decorator chains so concurrent/sequential builds overwrite imw.next causing wrong delegation and a data race. HOW: Return a new wrapper per call like ContextualLoggerMiddleware does, e.g. copy the struct and set next on the copy.

WHAT: QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics dereference req.PluginContext without the nil-req guard that LoggerMiddleware has. WHY: A nil request panics the backend plugin path instead of delegating to next. HOW: Add the same if req == nil { return m.next.X(ctx, req) } guard to each method.

WHAT: QueryData ranges over req.Queries and CallResource reads len(req.Body) without nil-req guards. WHY: A nil request panics where LoggerMiddleware explicitly delegates nil requests to next. HOW: Add if req == nil { return m.next.X(...) } guards matching LoggerMiddleware.

WHAT: instrumentPluginRequestSize/instrumentPluginRequest return plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered when the plugin is missing from the registry and callers return before invoking next. WHY: An observability lookup failure fails the functional plugin request (QueryData returns nil plus error) instead of best-effort metrics. HOW: Log the target-lookup error and still call next instead of returning early.

WHAT: LoggerMiddleware removed explicit pluginId, endpoint, dsName/dsUID, uname and traceID fields and relies solely on FromContext, but instrumentContext never adds traceID. WHY: Plugin Request Completed logs lose traceID correlation (and all fields when Logger is used without Contextual middleware first). HOW: Re-add traceID via tracing.TraceIDFromContext or make instrumentContext include it.

HELP text says 'returned' implying response size, but instrumentPluginRequestSize observes inbound sizes (len(Query.JSON), len(CallResource Body)). Users reading Prometheus HELP will misinterpret the metric. Remove 'returned'.

Missing nil-request guard causes panic: QueryData dereferences req.Queries, CallResource dereferences req.Body, CheckHealth/CollectMetrics dereference req.PluginContext. LoggerMiddleware in the same chain guards req==nil, proving nil is reachable. Add if req==nil passthrough before instrumenting, matching LoggerMiddleware.

Missing nil-request guard causes panic: all four methods dereference req.PluginContext via instrumentContext without checking req==nil. LoggerMiddleware guards this case so nil reaches the chain. Add if req==nil passthrough to next before calling instrumentContext in QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics.

logger_middleware.go removed explicit traceID log param assuming FromContext supplies it, but instrumentContext only adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname and never propagates tracing.TraceIDFromContext. Trace correlation in Plugin Request Completed logs is lost. Propagate traceID into WithContextualAttributes or retain explicit logging.

Incorrect measurement: float64(elapsed/time.Millisecond) divides Durations as int64 nanoseconds first, truncating sub-millisecond fractions to 0 and all other values down to whole ms. Buckets start at 0.005ms so precision matters, and the seconds histogram on the same request uses precise elapsed.Seconds(). Convert first: float64(elapsed)/float64(time.Millisecond). Applies to both Observe and ObserveWithExemplar paths.

Logic error: foundLabels is declared outside the per-metric loop and never reset, so counts accumulate across series; combined with returning an error on the first label-value mismatch instead of skipping that series, a family with more than one series will miscount or falsely fail. Reset the counter per metric and skip non-matching series.

The shouldInstrumentRequestSize=false cases (CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) are never asserted: the if at line 101 has no else, so if those endpoints incorrectly started emitting grafana_plugin_request_size_bytes the test would still pass. Add an else asserting CollectAndCount(metricRequestSize)==0.

issues.descricao: Claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil requests because it reads req.PluginContext without a nil guard.
Claims the refactor dropped traceID from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines.
Claims the metrics middleware factory mutates a shared instance's next field, causing a data race between chains.
Claims the request-size histogram's HELP text says 'returned' though it measures request sizes.
Claims the test never asserts that request size is not instrumented for CheckHealth/CollectMetrics.
Claims checkHistogram carries foundLabels across metrics and returns errors prematurely.
Claims millisecond durations are truncated by integer division before conversion to float.
Claims the request-size test cases use empty payloads and would not detect a broken size calculation.
Claims the duration metric checks only labels and sample counts, not the observed values.
Claims the duration-seconds histogram check omits status and source labels.
Claims LoggerMiddleware depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running first and would log without plugin identity if reordered.
Claims the metrics middleware now fails the request when the plugin is not in the registry.
The metrics middleware test never asserts that request size is not recorded for CheckHealth and CollectMetrics.

sugestoes.texto: Same obj pointer returned as created and read concurrently by background goroutine (likewise objInfo/options in Update); Storage impls mutate in place -> data race / torn legacy write. Deep-copy before handing to goroutine.

issues.descricao: Claims the Equal/NotEqual assertions in the Mode 3 tests can never fail, though the Equal assertion does fail if Delete stops returning the storage result.
Claims the legacy-create goroutine races with the caller on a shared obj that can alias the returned object.
Empty comment.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: initWatcher was moved to run after the lengthy search.init, so the broadcaster captures its since-RV only after indexing finishes. WHY: Writes committed during index building are invisible to Watch clients (gap in broadcast stream) whereas starting the watcher first buffered/replayed them; it also delays serving watches by the full index duration. HOW: Restore watcher-before-index order or capture the since-RV before indexing and replay deltas after.

issues.descricao: Claims the new postgres t.Skip removes coverage of the storage-server instrumentation test for that backend.
Claims making NewResourceServer call Init changes the constructor contract, blocking on the full index build and failing construction on any index error.
Claims starting the watcher after search.init makes writes between the index snapshot and initWatcher never reach the search index.
NewResourceServer now runs Init synchronously and fails construction on init error, blocking on index build and watcher startup and changing the constructor contract for callers.

NewResourceServer now runs Init synchronously (lifecycle, full search index build, watcher) and returns an error on failure, so callers that were not changed block on startup and abort construction on Init failure.
Claims write events arriving between search watcher start and initWatcher are consumed by the search reader and never reach Watch subscribers.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Loader now maps only promResponse rules and dropped matchRules Creating/Deleting handling. WHY: Transient deleting rules (prom-only) render as normal rows with full Edit/More actions instead of Deleting state without actions, and creating rules vanish. HOW: Restore operation-aware rendering for prom-only rows or filter/suppress actions while ruler/prom diverge.
Optional chain stops at .rules, so empty groups yields undefined.map() throw. Default to empty array: (groups.at(0)?.rules ?? []).map(...).

Comment states location is redundant in folder>group hierarchy but no showLocation={false} is passed and GrafanaRuleListItem defaults to true, so grouped rules show location contrary to declared intent.

issues.descricao: Claims provisioned status now comes from promRule.provenance, which the Prometheus response might omit, making provisioned rules editable.
Claims the promRule prop typed as Rule makes the Grafana prom-rule type guard return false for the GrafanaPromRuleDTO passed by GrafanaRuleListItem.
The menu test asserts exactly 4 menu items although the menuItems map also includes delete, so the count or comment may not match the real menu.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: grantType is snapshotted in the constructor but setFormParams() replaces formParams without updating it, and constructor NPEs on null formParams. WHY: Any path mutating form params leaves context.getGrantType() stale so OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse stores the wrong grant into the token ID; null params now crash where previously tolerated. HOW: Sync grantType in setFormParams() and null-guard the constructor lookup (or compute lazily from formParams).

WHAT: initToken unconditionally encodes the ID and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for any grantType with no registered shortcut. WHY: Custom/extension grants or any flow setting an unmapped grant string turn previously-successful token issuance into a 500 error. HOW: Fall back to rawTokenId (or UNKNOWN shortcut) when no shortcut is mapped instead of throwing.

issues.descricao: Claims setFormParams replaces form params without refreshing the cached grantType, leaving getGrantType() stale.
getShortcut() is added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation, breaking existing custom grant type factories when the encoder factory calls it.
Token context encoding calls getShouldUseLightweightToken on every token creation, which dereferences the session context client and would NPE where no client is set.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Reader thread busy-spins full listings with maxResults=Integer.MAX_VALUE and no throttle. WHY: Each iteration loads all groups with no pagination/backoff, creating unbounded request fanout and server load that can starve the deleter and destabilize the suite. HOW: Bound the page size and add backoff/yield between iterations.

issues.descricao: GroupAdapter's NPE guard is applied only to getSubGroupsCount; the getSubGroupsStream overloads still dereference modelSupplier.get(), which is null when the group is deleted concurrently.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The event listener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled() which in ClientPermissionsV2 unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: Deleting a client/role/group while ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is active crashes the removal flow instead of cleaning up. HOW: Skip V1 cleanup when V2 is enabled (V2 has no per-object permissions) or guard with !isFeatureEnabled(V2).

WHAT: canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles only check fine-grained permission and never check MANAGE_CLIENTS role, unlike canManage/canManageClientScopes siblings. WHY: A realm admin with manage-clients (or existing V1 behavior) is incorrectly denied role-mapping on clients, breaking the implied-admin contract.

WHAT: getClientsWithPermission calls root.evaluatePermission separately for every Clients-type resource inside findByType. WHY: Listing/filtering clients triggers O(N) full policy evaluations with N growing with client count, causing material slowdown on large realms.

setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but AdminPermissions still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled on ClientRemovedEvent. When clients() is V2 via MgmtPermissionsV2, any client deletion throws out of the event listener, aborting the transaction. Make it a no-op in V2 (no per-client state) or guard the listener for V2.

ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled now always throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions ProviderEventListener still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled on ClientRemovedEvent when fine-grained authz is enabled. In V2 that call will throw (breaking client deletion/event handling) instead of being a no-op. Guard the listener for V2 or make the V2 override a no-op.

issues.descricao: Claims the per-client resource lookup uses server.getId() as owner while resources are created with server.getClientId(), so client-specific permissions are never found.
Claims that with both fine-grained features enabled, client deletion calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims the all-clients resource lookup in hasPermission(String) cannot find the resource (owner mismatch or not lazily created), so global client permissions are ignored.
Claims the client management-permissions endpoint returns a 500 under V2 because it calls ClientPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims hasPermission(client, scope) accepts permissions granted on other resources because it does not filter by resource id, allowing privilege escalation across clients.
Claims getClientsWithPermission runs a separate policy evaluation for every client resource, causing O(N) slowdowns.
ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation for every client resource of type Clients, so listing clients costs one evaluation per client resource.

On ClientRemovedEvent the AdminPermissions listener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2 when V1 and V2 are both enabled, so client deletion fails.
Claims that with both fine-grained authz V1 and V2 enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which now throws, so client deletion fails.
Claims the test grants CONFIGURE together with MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, so addComposites may succeed because of CONFIGURE and the test would pass even if canMapCompositeRoles were broken.
Claims that under FGAP V2 the client management-permissions GET/PUT endpoints call the throwing ClientPermissionsV2 overrides and return 500.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError sets USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED on a fresh context.form() instance that is then discarded before rendering. sugestoes.texto: WHAT: getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check on the new BROKER_PUBLIC clause. WHY: any IdentityProviderModel with a null config map (e.g. newly constructed model before persistence) throws NPE when create/update/remove call registerIDPLoginInvalidation, breaking the write path.

WHY: with many organizations each distinct login query appends a new map entry to the same revisioned cache object, causing unbounded memory growth and larger replication payloads per realm.

Cache-hit path in getForLogin() returns raw getById() models while the miss/invalid path maps through createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. Resolve then wrap each cached IDP before adding, so both paths return the same enriched type.

issues.descricao: Claims getForLogin re-enters the caching layer by calling session.identityProviders().getById instead of idpDelegate.getById; this deliberately resolves IDs through the per-IDP cache.
Claims the cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw, non-organization-aware models; getById already wraps them.
Claims linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization never invalidates the getForLogin caches; the org provider routes through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update which does.
Claims resolving cached IDs one by one with getById turns login listing into N lookups; those lookups hit the per-IDP cache by design.
Claims the HashSet in cached getForLogin returns IDPs in nondeterministic order; every caller sorts the result.
Claims remove() of a nonexistent alias now dereferences null; the new login invalidation is null-safe and the other call is unchanged pre-existing code.
Claims getLoginPredicate can NPE on a null config; config is always initialized.

getForLogin caches all organizations under one realm/mode entry, so each new organizationId invalidates and rebuilds that entry with every previously cached search merged in, instead of caching per organization.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: update() reads validated_data.get("detector_type") but the serializer field is `type` (validated by validate_type) and create() uses validated_data["type"]. WHY: the lookup always misses and falls back to instance.group_type, so detector type changes via PUT are silently ignored. HOW: read validated_data.get("type", instance.group_type).

WHAT: column fallback reads tableData?.meta.fields but only guards tableData, so meta===undefined throws TypeError while data uses tableData?.data ?? []. WHY: any empty/partial TabularData (e.g. the empty placeholder above) crashes render instead of showing an empty table. HOW: guard meta with tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {}.

WHAT: analytics.record fires before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check. WHY: disabled-flag and rejected requests pollute analytics and record user/project IDs for requests that should be no-ops. HOW: move the record call after the feature gate.

WHAT: tag.key (which can be tags[...,number] or contain slashes/spaces) is interpolated directly into the request path. WHY: keys with / break routing to a wrong endpoint and brackets/commas produce malformed URLs, letting crafted attribute names alter the request target. HOW: encode with encodeURIComponent(attributeKey).

WHAT: the endpoint loops over an attacker-controlled unauthenticated raw_data list with no size cap, validating each item and emitting metrics. WHY: a single request with a huge array burns CPU on DRF validation and fans out unbounded metrics.incr calls, enabling cheap request-amplification DoS. HOW: enforce a max batch size before the loop.

issues.descricao: Claims the unauthenticated endpoint iterates an unbounded array of reports, allowing CPU/metric-spam DoS.
Claims BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns Django HttpResponse objects although its Endpoint base expects DRF Response objects.
The assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check, so requests rejected with 404 are still counted as assemble events, skewing analytics.
BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update() reads validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of 'type', so detector type changes are silently ignored.

Claims the triggered_actions log now writes the full event payload with user data because event_data was switched to workflow_event_data.
Claims the success path dereferences data.summary without guarding undefined data when the query is disabled or errored.
Claims the column fallback crashes when tableData is defined but meta is missing.
Claims ExploreParams still reads visualize.yAxes after the Visualize class switched to yAxis, producing undefined saved-query params.
Asks to verify that no caller passes Visualize instances instead of BaseVisualize to updateLocationWithAggregateFields.
Claims the number-type test's mock matches query.query instead of substringMatch, so its not-called assertion can never fail.
Claims the attribute key is interpolated into the request path without encodeURIComponent, enabling path confusion.
get_environment_info fetches the recommended event per issue while building the merged-PR comment, an N+1 lookup on the comment path.
The number-type test mock matches on query.query while the hook sends substringMatch, so the mock can never match and the not-called assertion cannot fail.
Claims _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, so PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title raises AttributeError.
Claims the hook now returns undefined attributes before the first fetch instead of {}, which can crash consumers that access keys on the TagCollection.
Claims the default of sentry:autofix_automation_tuning changed from low to off, silently disabling automatic autofix for projects that never set it, unrelated to the replays bulk delete feature.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `to_dict()` via `asdict` keeps `queued` as a raw datetime, which is passed as celery `apply_async` kwargs in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`. WHY: the datetime is not JSON-serializable so outbound assignee sync tasks fail to serialize/enqueue instead of syncing. HOW: serialize `queued` to isoformat string in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

WHAT: `from_dict` passes a serialized `queued` string straight into a datetime field with no coercion, and returns None on any unexpected/missing key. WHY: a None source makes `should_sync(..., None)` return True, silently disabling the cycle guard the PR adds and resuming the loop. HOW: coerce/validate `queued`, `source_name`, and `integration_id` explicitly as above.

WHAT: base `sync_status_outbound` adds explicit `assignment_source` param but `ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` accepts no **kwargs. WHY: any caller passing `assignment_source=` to that installation raises TypeError, breaking the override contract. HOW: keep the new param absorbed via **kwargs on the base or update all overrides to accept it.

to_dict() returns raw datetime in queued via asdict, passed as assignment_source_dict to apply_async kwargs. Celery JSON encoder has no rule for datetime so enqueue raises. Serialize to ISO string and parse back in from_dict, use default_factory for queued.

to_dict() leaves queued as datetime but it is sent through Celery apply_async kwargs which must be JSON-serializable and read back by from_dict() with no ISO-string parsing. Serialize queued to isoformat (and parse back in from_dict) so outbound assignee sync does not fail serialization or round-trip as wrong type.

issues.descricao: Claims to_dict() returns a raw datetime for queued that fails JSON serialization when passed as Celery task kwargs.
The assignment_source parameter was added to the abstract sync_status_outbound instead of sync_assignee_outbound, which is the method that actually receives it.
Claims concrete integrations overriding should_sync(self, attribute) will raise TypeError at the new two-argument call in sync_assignee_outbound.
Claims a malformed assignment_source_dict makes from_dict return None, so should_sync fails open and re-enables the sync cycle.
test_to_dict asserts queued is not None, which is always true because queued has a default, so the assertion verifies nothing.
Claims passing AssignmentSource.to_dict() with a raw datetime to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async fails Sentry's bad-pickle check in tests and would break under a JSON serializer.

sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter that is never threaded through the status task or checked in should_sync, so status sync gets no cycle prevention despite the signature suggesting it.

Claims getSlots uses the optional override.timeZone, so an override without it passes undefined to dayjs.tz and computes a wrong offset using the server timezone.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: getCalendarCredentials calls async getCalendar without await, storing a Promise in the calendar field while remaining a sync function. WHY: Any caller other than the patched getConnectedCalendars that uses calendar.listCalendars/createEvent directly gets a Promise object, causing runtime TypeError and broken calendar listing/booking. sugestoes.texto: WHAT: emailValidation depends on `rejectedEmails.@each` while the array holds primitive strings pushed via `pushObject`. WHY: `@each` observes properties of array items, not membership, so pushing a blocked email does not invalidate the computed property and the error is not shown until the email field itself changes. HOW: Depend on `rejectedEmails.[]` (or `rejectedEmails.length) instead of `rejectedEmails.@each`.

Comment claims last_match_at indicates 'have ever been blocked', but BlockedEmail.should_block? updates match_count/last_match_at for every match including action_type :do_nothing (proven by shared examples for both :block and :do_nothing). A do_nothing hit sets last_match_at without blocking, so the prose is untrue. Fix the comment to say matched/seen, not blocked.

BlockedEmail.should_block? returns nil instead of false when the email has no record.
Claims EmailValidator dropped the email format check that the old User#email_validator performed, allowing invalid emails.

WHY: Any email built with add_unsubscribe_link:true without unsubscribe_url raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fails to send. Triple-brace {{{...}}} disables escaping for a string built from I18n topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications interpolated with model.fancyTitle. Neighbouring line uses {{i18n ...}} (escaped). If the title contains HTML, it is injected into the page. Use double braces or escape the title before interpolation.

Provide a fallback or keep old template working when unsubscribe_url is absent.

Claims the unsubscribe page renders the topic title unescaped through triple braces, allowing HTML injection.

The unsubscribe_link string now requires unsubscribe_url, so any MessageBuilder caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without it would raise a missing-interpolation error.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: URI without a scheme has nil host, so website_name returns nil even when website is present. WHY: The template gates on {{#if model.website_name}}, so a stored value like example.com/user disappears instead of showing fallback host text. issues.descricao: The www.example.com vs forum.example.com branch of website_name is not tested.
The scheme-less website case (nil host) of website_name is not tested.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Switching from interpolateVariablesInQueries to applyTemplateVariables drops the datasource:getRef() assignment. WHY: Old method (datasource.ts:436-438) stamped each query with datasource ref; new method (datasource.ts:1135-1140) returns only expr/step/legendFormat, leaving stale/missing datasource on split targets for downstream routing. Notes test coverage of shard interpolation; no issue.

runShardSplitQuery now uses applyTemplateVariables, which strips __auto/__range scoped vars, so queries with [$__auto] reach shard sub-requests uninterpolated and fail.

sugestoes.texto: DB stub changed behaviour contract: RunCommands/QueryFramesInto/TablesList previously executed real in-memory DuckDB work and callers (parser.go TablesList, sql_command.go NewSQLCommand/Execute) rely on success. Now every call returns 'not implemented', so all SQL expressions unconditionally fail. Either restore real implementation or update consumers to handle disabled state.

New pkg/expr/sql.DB stub returns 'not implemented' for TablesList/RunCommands/QueryFramesInto, but sql_command.go:100 and parser.go:26 call them expecting real results. After replacing duck.NewInMemoryDB, every SQL Execute/TablesList fails — output never matches expected behavior.

Name NewInMemoryDB promises the working in-memory DB callers in parser.go and sql_command.go expect from duck.NewInMemoryDB, but the new type holds no state and every method returns 'not implemented'. Rename to reflect stub status (e.g. NewStubDB/NewDisabledDB) or document that it is intentionally unimplemented so callers are not misled.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go provides QueryFramesInto that unconditionally returns not implemented, while pkg/expr/sql_command.go now calls sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto expecting it to populate the result frame. Every SQLCommand.Execute therefore fails. Implement the DB methods (restore duck-backed logic) instead of stubbing.

issues.descricao: enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the sqlExpressions feature flag, so SQL expressions are rejected unconditionally.
The go-duck DB was replaced by a stub whose methods always return 'not implemented', so table parsing and SQL expression execution always fail.
Claims the rejection message says 'not implemented' though the guard is a feature-flag check.
Garbled request to update db.go to use sql.NewInMemoryDB().
Vague claim that the query interface changed and lines 96 and 100 need updating.
enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path (the flag is negated and both branches return false), so SQL expressions are rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.
Claims TablesList now calls a stub that always errors, so existing parser tests in pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go would break.
The TypeSQL branch in nodes.go reaches UnmarshalSQLCommand → NewSQLCommand → DuckDB parsing without the enableSqlExpressions check, leaving the SQL expression RCE/LFI path reachable.
Existing SQL tests in sql_command_test.go calling NewSQLCommand would now fail because the stubbed DB's TablesList returns 'not implemented', and they were not updated.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Check returns deny from permDenialCache before trying cached perms or the DB requery, and the entry is never cleared when access is later granted. WHY: A deny cached at T blocks the fresh-DB fallback added in the same PR until TTL expiry, so newly granted dashboards/folders stay denied and the PR goal is defeated. HOW: Delete the denial key on allow (or only set/check it on the DB path miss) instead of short-circuiting unconditionally.

WHAT: A denial entry is stored per (namespace, user, action, name, parent) where name/parent are request-controlled, in a local cache with only TTL expiry. WHY: Enumerating random resource names creates one entry per guess and grows memory/serialization load per user until expiry, turning a cheap deny into a cache-blowup vector. HOW: Omit if speculative — verifier to confirm local-cache bounds; otherwise bound cardinality (e.g. cap entries, hash, or cache negative action-level results only).

issues.descricao: Claims a cached denial blocks access granted within the TTL window; denials are TTL-bounded like the existing permission cache.
Claims trusting cached grants while re-checking cached denials lets stale grants keep access to revoked resources; cached grants were already served for the TTL before this PR.
Claims per-resource denial entries cause unbounded cache memory growth; entries expire after the short TTL.
Claims List now serves stale cached permissions whereas it previously always queried the DB; List was already cache-backed before the change.

Claims the new denial cache is checked before any permission source and never invalidated, so a Check that ran before a resource was created or a grant was added keeps returning Allowed:false for the whole short cache TTL.
Claims the remote authz client still wraps results in a 30s LocalCache, so in remote deployments new dashboards, folders and grants stay invisible for up to 30s.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: MaxCount cleanup fetches victim IDs with LIMIT/OFFSET then deletes them in a separate statement with no transaction. WHY: Concurrent deletion of newer rows between fetch and delete shifts the OFFSET window, so a fetched ID can slide back into the top-MaxCount set that must be kept yet still gets deleted. HOW: Re-check membership or perform the delete atomically if exact MaxCount retention is required.

untilDoneOrCancelled stops when batchWork returns affected==0, but batchWork now returns RowsAffected from deleteByIDs after a separate fetchIDs with LIMIT. Under concurrent deletes the fetched IDs can already be gone so delete affects 0 even though unfetched matching rows remain beyond the LIMIT window, causing early exit with MaxAge/MaxCount/orphan invariant still violated. Terminate on fetched count == 0 instead of deleted count == 0.

issues.descricao: Empty comment with no claim.
Garbled text on the cleanup ticker line with no identifiable claim.
Claims the SQLite-limit regression test never sends more than 32,766 parameters to an annotation DELETE because the fixtures are split across three types.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: readSequence subtracts child TLV sizes from declared length but never requires exactly zero and never checks trailing bytes, and maps indefinite length (-1) to empty sequence. WHY: Malformed DER with over-read children or trailing garbage is accepted as valid, breaking DER strictness relied on by ECDSA conversions.

WHAT: AuthzClient.create calls global CryptoIntegration.init which initializes a static singleton only once with the authz classloader view. WHY: If called before server init with a classloader seeing only the order-100 Authz provider, the server is permanently pinned to the weak provider whose methods throw UnsupportedOperationException.

integerToBytes slices off high-order bytes without validating sign or size. A negative DER INTEGER (e.g. 02 01 FF -> BigInteger -1) is left-padded to a large positive value, and an oversized positive (>qLength bytes) is silently truncated to its low qLength bytes instead of rejected. Verify s.signum()>=0 and that bytes.length<=qLength+1 with leading-zero padding before slicing; throw IOException otherwise.

readSequence subtracts each TLV length from the declared SEQUENCE length but never checks for negative remainder or leftover bytes. An inner INTEGER whose TLV extends past the parent length makes length negative and the loop exits silently, and trailing garbage after a correctly-sized SEQUENCE (outer length < total input) is ignored because remaining bytes are never checked. Reject length<0 and trailing bytes so malformed DER signatures are not accepted as valid r||s.

issues.descricao: Claims getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle; that is the intended fallback for the BC-free authz client.
Claims readLength's -1 for indefinite-length encoding breaks length arithmetic or array allocation; the decoder only parses locally generated DER and the sequence path already rejects it.
Claims the lenient sequence parser allows malformed or trailing DER and signature malleability in verification; the parser never sees external signatures.
Claims integerToBytes can silently truncate oversized INTEGER values; inputs come from local signing and always fit the component width.
Claims createECParams/getKeyFactory throwing UnsupportedOperationException breaks EC JWK parsing in the authz client; the client does not use that path.

ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes the -1 returned by readLength for indefinite-length encoding to read(int), which allocates new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException on malformed DER input.
integerToBytes silently truncates r/s values longer than the curve size, so non-canonical DER signatures are accepted as different values (signature malleability).
AuthzClient.create eagerly initializes CryptoIntegration, so a shaded/repackaged client that lost its ServiceLoader file fails at construction instead of only when ECDSA is used.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: canView(user)/canManage(user) dropped ADMIN role from hasOneAdminRole check. WHY: Admins relying on ADMIN role lose view/manage access (denial) diverging from prior contract and V1 behavior. HOW: Restore AdminRoles.ADMIN in the role checks or prove ADMIN is handled elsewhere.

issues.descricao: Claims removing the canView filter from searchForUser lets admins see users they are not allowed to view.
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission scans group resources and evaluates permissions for each on every user search or count request.
Claims deleting a group under V2 triggers the removal listener, which calls GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims testManageGroupMembership never exercises the group-level manage-membership permission.
searchForUser no longer filters results with usersEvaluator::canView, so an admin with query access but no view permission and no group grants gets an unrestricted user list.

GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) does not fall back to canView(), and the PR dropped the canViewGlobal short-circuit, so an admin with an all-groups VIEW permission is denied (and the group filtered out of listings) for any group that has its own permission resource lacking VIEW.
Claims GroupResource management-permissions endpoints call GroupPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException, causing 500s when V2 is active.

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission does not restrict evaluated permissions to the evaluated resource, so when falling back to the all-groups resource a permission granted on one specific group can satisfy the check for any group.

GroupsResource.getGroups no longer hoists the global canView() check, so in FGAP V2 each listed group triggers its own resource lookup and policy evaluation even when an all-groups grant would cover them all.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is renumbered from 4 to 3 while the old value 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. WHY: Existing automation keyed on exit code 4 for recreate-upgrade misclassifies results after upgrade (3 now means recreate, 4 now means feature-disabled). HOW: Keep RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE at 4 and assign FEATURE_DISABLED a fresh code (e.g. 3) to preserve the established contract.

issues.descricao: Claims the rolling-updates feature is not enabled for the null update strategy in UpgradeTest, so that case tests the operator without the gated feature.
Claims RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 and 4 now means feature disabled, a breaking change that needs release notes.
Claims calling picocli.exit() for the disabled-feature exit code is incorrect because it calls System.exit directly.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Constructor calls credentialModelOpt.get() with no presence check, throwing NoSuchElementException when no federated or local recovery-codes credential exists. WHY: Crashes recovery-code login rendering instead of failing with a handled error, newly reachable when a storage provider accepts updateCredential but exposes nothing via getCredentials.

issues.descricao: Claims the recovery-code validator uses non-constant-time String.equals, leaking timing information about stored codes.
Claims raw recovery codes are serialized and persisted in cleartext in user storage instead of hashed.
Claims Optional.get() on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without isPresent() can throw NoSuchElementException.
Plaintext recovery codes are serialized and sent to user storage providers via updateCredential, while the local path stores only hashed codes.
Recovery codes are sent to user storage providers in plaintext instead of hashed, so a provider may persist working second-factor codes.
The test user storage accepts any of the user's recovery codes rather than the specific requested code number, unlike the local provider.
BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, so it throws NullPointerException for a user missing from the provider's map.

sugestoes.texto: start_offset is clamped with max(0,offset) but the is_prev trimming check at line 192 compares len(results)==offset+limit+extra using raw offset. With offset<0 the fetched window is larger than the compared value by |offset|, so the extra-row trim never triggers (or triggers wrongly for is_prev path which still passes negative offset to slice). Use start_offset consistently or reject negative offsets.

start_offset is computed from offset (clamped with max(0,offset)) and used for slicing, but the prev-page boundary check still uses the original offset. When clamping applies the length comparison is off, causing incorrect trimming/reversing and wrong pagination results. Use start_offset in the len() comparison.

issues.descricao: Claims the prev-page trim check uses the raw offset instead of the clamped start_offset, so clamped or negative offsets mis-trim results and return wrong page boundaries.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator relies on self.key and self._is_asc that only DateTimePaginator defines, so get_item_key raises AttributeError.
Claims the audit log endpoint imports an OptimizedCursorPaginator class that does not exist.
The prev-cursor trimming check still uses the raw offset instead of start_offset, so when they differ it drops or keeps the wrong row.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True for the errors dataset while upsampled_count is only registered in DiscoverDatasetConfig. WHY: An allowlisted errors-dataset stats query is rewritten to upsampled_count() which the errors resolver cannot resolve, failing the query instead of upsampling. HOW: Remove the errors fast-path or register an equivalent upsampled_count function for the errors dataset path.

Presence of client_sample_rate is tested with truthiness (`if client_sample_rate:`), so a legitimate value of 0 / 0.0 is treated as missing and sample_rate is never set. Use an explicit existence check instead so 0 propagates as float 0.0

issues.descricao: The test factory helper uses a truthiness check on client_sample_rate, so a rate of 0.0 is not copied to sample_rate (claimed to silently drop a legitimate value).
Claims cache keys for upsampling eligibility are built with Python's hash() and cannot be invalidated across workers; no such cache exists.
Claims changing the topEvents validation message breaks consumers asserting the old 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' text; none exist.
Comment reports no problem.
Comment reports no problem.
Comment reports no problem.
Comment reports no problem.
Claims the factory writes sample_rate while upsampled_count reads sample_weight, so the upsampled count would be 1 instead of 10.
upsampled_count is registered only in DiscoverDatasetConfig, so if the errors dataset resolves functions through another config, the upsampled_count() query fails as an unknown function.
Inline test comments say each bucket has 1 event while the assertions expect count == 10, contradicting the upsampled value.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: _get_partition_lock reads/writes partition_locks dict without any global lock, so two threads adding a new partition can create two different Lock objects. WHY: Threads then guard add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable with different locks, breaking mutual exclusion and corrupting all_offsets/outstanding commit decisions. HOW: Guard lock creation with a global lock for partition_locks.

WHAT: get_committable_offsets iterates range(start, max_offset+1) covering every gap offset, plus min/max over the whole set each second. WHY: When head-of-line is blocked all_offsets grows unbounded and a sparse range (e.g. missing offsets, retention jumps) makes each 1s commit poll O(range) CPU, stalling the commit thread. HOW: Iterate only sorted known offsets instead of the full integer range.

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit passes FilteredPayload to decoder and expects None to skip+commit. The wired decoder partial(self.decode_payload,...) asserts not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload), so filtered messages raise AssertionError into the generic except instead of the intended None fast-path (error log + reliance on exception fallback). Guard FilteredPayload before delegating to decode_payload.

issues.descricao: Claims queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown() are unavailable on Python < 3.13, so workers never exit on shutdown.
Claims Python's randomized str hash makes group-to-queue assignment differ across processes, breaking per-subscription ordering and letting two processes handle the same subscription concurrently.
Claims FixedQueuePool.submit leaks an outstanding offset when put() raises after add_offset, permanently blocking commits for the partition.
Claims get_stats/wait_until_empty report empty while items are still in flight because qsize drops when a worker takes an item.
Claims metrics.incr receives len(committable) as the instance argument instead of the amount, so the commit count is always 1.
The offsets_committed metric is incremented by the number of partitions being committed rather than the number of offsets, so its name misdescribes the value.
Claims factory shutdown leaves SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy commit threads running and committing after shutdown.
Claims the committable-offset loop iterates the whole numeric span max_offset - start, burning CPU on large offset gaps every commit cycle.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: process_batch indexes val["end_timestamp_precise"] directly with no fallback. WHY: A single span event missing the field raises KeyError and aborts the whole ValuesBatch in buffer.process_spans (poison-pill/consumer stall). HOW: Use .get with fallback/clamp instead of direct indexing.

WHAT: Untrusted SDK-controlled end_timestamp_precise is used verbatim as the ZSET score driving ZPOPMIN eviction. WHY: An attacker can send far-future timestamps to pin their spans and force eviction of legitimate spans in the same segment, biasing sampling/storage. HOW: Validate/clamp the score server-side instead of trusting client time.

WHAT: Every span insert runs up to two ZUNIONSTORE full copies of the up-to-1000-member set plus ZCARD/ZPOPMIN. WHY: Building a segment span-by-span copies O(N) per insert, i.e. O(N^2) total per segment and O(B*N) per batch in the ingest hot path. HOW: Merge once per batch or skip union when keys are already joined.

issues.descricao: Claims the redirect-resolution limit was silently cut from 10000 to 1000, so segment trees deeper than 1000 are no longer joined, and the comment still mentions 10k.
Claims a non-root span whose key equals the resolved set key unions the key with itself and then unlinks it, deleting the buffered segment.
Claims a span message missing end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError and aborts the whole batch.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch passes cursor.offset directly into queryset slicing when advanced features are enabled.
Claims BasePaginator.get_result sets start_offset to an unclamped offset for previous-page cursors, allowing negative slicing.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies floor/ceil to a datetime key, raising TypeError.
Claims accessing organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError when organization_context is None.
process_batch indexes end_timestamp_precise directly, so a span without the field raises KeyError and fails the whole consumer batch.
Claims span_count counts pre-existing spans in set_key, so zpopmin evicts far more than the overflow above 1000 and discards valid spans.
